successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy entity interface is exported with all specified fields and correct types (id, policyName, leaveType as LeaveType, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt), importing LeaveType from src/shared/types/index.ts.

The repository interface exposes six methods with correct signatures: findById(id)→LeavePolicy|null, findByLeaveType(leaveType)→LeavePolicy|null, findAllActive()→LeavePolicy[], create(Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>)→LeavePolicy, update(id, Partial<Omit<...>>)→LeavePolicy|null, deactivate(id)→boolean.

create() persists a new leave_policies row with a generated UUID id and current timestamps, and returns the mapped LeavePolicy entity; it throws a typed error when the insert returns no row or a row that fails the type guard.
findByLeaveType() returns the single active LeavePolicy for a given leave type (filtering is_active = true) or null when none exists; findAllActive() returns only policies where is_active = true.

update() with partial input persists only the provided fields, always bumps updated_at, and returns the updated entity or null on not-found; when no fields are provided it falls back to findById and returns the current record.
deactivate() sets is_active = false and updated_at to now, and returns true when a row was affected (rowCount > 0) or false when the id was not found.
Rows that fail the type guard are rejected safely: findById and update return null, findByLeaveType and findAllActive skip them, and create throws rather than returning an invalid entity.
No `any` type appears anywhere in the module; the type guard narrows from `unknown` without casting to `any`, and the row interface uses an index signature with `unknown`-compatible values.
Unit tests cover found, not-found, type-guard-failure, and DB-error cases for each repository method, mocking pool.query and asserting SQL text contains the expected table and clause fragments.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001); the repository implementation must extend BaseRepository from src/shared/base-repository.ts and issue SQL via its query helper — no direct pool.query calls in the repository class itself.
No `any` type anywhere (HARNESS constraint no-any); use `unknown` with type guards for row validation, mirroring the Employee repository's isEmployeeRow pattern.
The repository must import LeaveType from src/shared/types/index.ts and type the leaveType field/column against that enum — no local redefinition of the enum.

The DB table is leave_policies with snake_case columns; the row mapper must convert snake_case DB columns to camelCase entity fields and vice versa for create/update, matching the Employee repository convention.

IDs must be generated with randomUUID() and timestamps with new Date() at create time, matching the Employee repository pattern; the repository does not rely on DB defaults for id/createdAt/updatedAt.

Unit tests must mock the pool from src/shared/db/connection before importing the repository, cast pool.query as jest.Mock, and reset it in beforeEach — matching the Employee repository test structure.
outOfScope: LeavePolicyService, ILeavePolicyService, controllers, routes, and RBAC wiring — these belong to Phase 8 (services) and Phase 10 (routes), not this repository/model phase.
Database migrations or schema DDL for the leave_policies table — this phase defines the model and repository only; migrations are handled separately.

A leave_types table, leave_type_id FK, or a leave-types module — the settled decision stores leaveType directly as a string column holding the LeaveType enum value; no such table or module exists or is planned.
Audit logging (GP-002) within the repository — the repository is a data-access layer; audit records are written by the service layer in later phases, not by the repository itself.
Input validation (GP-003) — validation at API boundaries is a service/controller concern in later phases; the repository accepts already-shaped domain input.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle is ACTIVE/INACTIVE governed by the isActive boolean; deactivate() transitions a policy to inactive (is_active = false) and is the only state-changing operation in this phase — there is no hard delete, only deactivation.

Each leave type maps to a single active LeavePolicy; findByLeaveType returns at most one record (the first active row for that leave type), reflecting the architecture's one-active-policy-per-leave-type rule.

createdAt and updatedAt are set to the current time on creation and updatedAt is always bumped on any update or deactivation; the repository never accepts caller-supplied id, createdAt, or updatedAt (they are Omit'd from create and update input types).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the LeavePolicy or null when not found or when the row fails the type guard; propagates underlying database errors without swallowing them.
Returns the single active LeavePolicy for the given leave type or null when none exists or the row fails the type guard; propagates database errors.
Returns an array of active LeavePolicy entities, filtering out any rows that fail the type guard; returns an empty array when none exist; propagates database errors.

Persists a new row with a generated UUID and current timestamps and returns the mapped entity; throws a typed Error when the insert returns no row or a row failing the type guard; propagates database errors.

Persists only provided fields, always bumps updated_at, returns the updated entity or null on not-found/type-guard failure; falls back to findById returning the current record when no fields are provided; propagates database errors.
Sets is_active=false and updated_at=now; returns true when a row was affected (rowCount > 0) or false when the id was not found; propagates database errors.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The repository implementation must mirror the Employee repository structure: a private row interface with snake_case columns and an index signature, a rowToEntity mapper, an isEntityRow type guard narrowing from unknown without any, a private inner class extending BaseRepository instantiated as this.base, hand-written SQL via this.base.query, randomUUID() for IDs, new Date() for timestamps, and a dynamic SET-clause builder with a paramIndex counter for update.

The LeaveType enum (annual | sick | emergency | unpaid | maternity | paternity) must be imported from src/shared/types/index.ts and used as the type of LeavePolicy.leaveType; the model must not redefine the enum locally.

The repository must extend BaseRepository (via a private inner class) and use its generic query<T extends Record<string, unknown>> helper for all SQL; it must not call pool.query directly or bypass the repository pattern.

The unit test must follow the Employee repository test structure: jest.mock the db connection pool before importing the repository, cast pool.query as jest.Mock, provide makeRow (snake_case) and makeEntity (camelCase) helpers, reset the mock in beforeEach, and assert SQL text contains expected table/clause fragments for each method.

The repository interface must use the same Omit/Partial<Omit> create/update signature convention as IEmployeeRepository — create accepts Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'> and update accepts Partial<Omit<LeavePolicy,'id'|'createdAt'|'updatedAt'>>.

integrationPoints.why: Imports the LeaveType enum used to type LeavePolicy.leaveType; this is the sole cross-module dependency for the leave-policy module per the reconciled dependency map (leave-policy → shared-types).
The repository implementation extends BaseRepository to inherit the generic query helper and pool access; required by the repository-pattern constraint (GP-001) and the Employee module template.
The pool is consumed transitively via BaseRepository; unit tests mock this module's pool export before importing the repository, matching the Employee test pattern.

The Employee repository is the direct structural template for the LeavePolicy repository (row interface, mapper, type guard, base class, SQL style, update SET-clause builder, create error throw); the implementation and tests must be structurally consistent with it.
